subject.title: Feature: Per-mention model routing + context window for group mentions

question: Should mention-state group processing become a first-class shared routing contract, or should core expose a trusted pre-gating plugin hook and leave background-model behavior to an optional plugin?
rationale: The choice changes the security boundary for unmentioned messages, public configuration surface, provider precedence, and ownership split between core routing and channel plugins; source inspection cannot determine the intended product policy.

options.title: Add shared activation contract
options.body: Introduce a generic mention-state and bounded-context routing contract, with background processing disabled by default and consistent precedence across channel plugins.

options.title: Expose trusted plugin hook
options.body: Add a read-only or policy-limited pre-gating hook so an optional plugin can implement background classification without channel-specific core configuration.

options.title: Ship context buffering only
options.body: Add per-group bounded mention context while deferring all background-model processing and its larger trust-boundary decision.

recommendation.title: Add shared activation contract
recommendation.body: Introduce a generic mention-state and bounded-context routing contract, with background processing disabled by default and consistent precedence across channel plugins.
